## Week 4
### Bernoulli Random Variables
Can only take values {0,1} and has a single parameter $0\le p\le 1$.
The same as a Binomial with $n = 1$

$p_X(x) = 1-p$  if x=0
$p_X(x) = p$  if x=1

$\mu = E(X)=p$
$E(X^2)=p$
$\sigma^2 = Var(X) = p − p2 = p(1 − p)$

# Uniform Random Variables

# Binomial Random Variable
$X \sim Bin(n,p)$
$X_i \sim Bernoulli(p)$
$X = X_1+X_2+...+X_n$
$E(X)=E(X_1)+E(X_2)+...+E(X_n)$
$= p+p+...+p$
$= np$
$Var(X) = Var(x_1)+...+Var(X_n)$
The event $X=x$ occurs when $x$ trials result in successes and $n-x$ trials result in failure.
## Factorials
How many ways are there to organise $r$ objects in order, if chosen from a pool of $n$ objects.
Thus there are $n$ choices for the first position, $(n-1)$ for the second and so on until $(n-r+1)$ for the last.
$$\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}$$
$$\left({n \atop r}\right) = \frac{n!}{r!\times(n-r)!}$$
## Example
A flood occurs with $p=0.1$, not more than 1 occurs per year.
Over 5 years what is the:
Expected number of floods --> $5\times0.1=0.5$
chance of 3 floods = $\P(X=3)=({5\atop3})(0.1)^3\times(0.9)^2=0.0081$
$\P(X > 0)=1−\P(X = 0)=1−\left({5\atop0}\right)(0.1)^0\times(0.9)^5 = 0.41.$
